ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and shareholders against the PEP lists maintained by the CBE Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-EG), the Unified Sanctions List of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN Sanctions List, and the European Union Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required if any match is flagged; additionally, negative news and FATF mutual evaluation publication screening is performed. All screening evidence must be retained for at least five years post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI 'Start & Invest' (registration.investment.gov.eg) and the GAFI Investor Services Center; name reservation also available through the GAFI mobile application
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory company name must be composed in Arabic script (Article 6 of the Executive Regulations of the Companies Law). A Latin-script transliteration is permitted for internal operational use, but the official name registered in the Commercial Registry is recorded only in Arabic. For LLCs, Arabic name must contain the legal form indicator 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' (LLC). Must be phonetically transliterated into Arabic without any semantic inconsistency. Foreign names may be derived from a transliteration of the overseas entity name, but the transliteration must not violate public order or religious symbols.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerial approval required for: 'Arab', 'Egypt', 'Union', 'United', 'Central', 'Bank', 'National', 'Federal', 'Islamic', 'Coptic', 'Army', 'State', 'Public', 'Supreme' and any term implying government sponsorship or sovereign affiliation

Prohibited absolute tokens: obscene or offensive terms under Egyptian Penal Code Article 178, terms referencing narcotics, alcoholic beverages, gambling, or escort services, and those that mimic political party names, illegal organizations, or religious slogans
Prohibited use of any registered mark resembling an existing trade name in the same activity class (ISIC 7310)
Restricted tokens: 'Media', 'Press', 'Broadcast', 'Advertising' unless the applicant produces the required sectoral license/certificate or approval from the Supreme Council for Media Regulation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon issuance of a formal rejection notice by GAFI, the applicant may file a written administrative Appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 days of rejection. The appeal must include a detailed counter-argument demonstrating compliance with the naming rules (Executive Regulations of Companies Law, Chapter 2). A fee of EGP 1,000 (approx. USD 20) is required. The Legal Affairs Department must respond within 30 business days. If the appeal is rejected, the applicant may proceed to the Administrative Judiciary Court under Article 24 of the State Council Law No. 47 of 1972. The entire appeal timeline should not exceed 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance. Egypt's Commercial Registry and Tax Authority require a physical local address for LLCs with an operational license. A registered agent may be used for a virtual office, but the company must have a local representative physically co-located at the virtual office to receive litigation service and tax inspections. The virtual office is acceptable for the low-risk ISIC 7310 agency segment only if: (i) the virtual office provider is licensed as a serviced office operator under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; (ii) the registered lease contract (lease agreement) is submitted to GAFI, and (iii) the company's management arranges at least a quarterly presence for physical meetings and document inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk (approx. 15%) for low-risk standard industry; GAFI may perform unannounced physical verification within the first 12 months of incorporation. Additionally, the Commercial Registry office may randomly conduct a compliance visit under Law 34/2011 on Commercial Registry Oversight. In practice, the inspection likelihood increases to 30% when the company uses a virtual office or serviced premises outside a traditional commercial building complex.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egypt Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Joint-Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares, and Limited Liability Companies), as amended by Law No. 180 of 2018, Arts. 74-97 (LLC regime); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (PM Decree No. 2310 of 2017); commercial registration administered through GAFI's integrated window.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Incorporation and Registration Directorate, Integrated One-Stop Shop (Cairo and governorate branches), acting with the Commercial Register of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contract of Incorporation and Statute (Articles of Association), drafted in Arabic, signed by all quota-holders, authenticated by the Notary Public (Real Estate Publicity and Notarization Authority), and filed electronically through GAFI's incorporation e-service for entry into the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs after the 2018 amendments; founders remain free to set nominal capital (market standard EGP 50,000). Quotas must be fully subscribed by founders; in-cash quotas must be funded into the company bank account at or promptly after incorporation. No escrow or consignment account is imposed on LLCs (a bank deposit certificate is required only for joint-stock companies under Law No. 159 of 1981).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding quota-holders, by unanimous written resolution, resolve as follows. One: the Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association of the Company, as submitted to GAFI, are adopted in full. Two: each quota-holder subscribes to the quotas allocated in Schedule A; the entire paid-up capital is represented by cash contributions deposited in the Company's bank account. Three: the registered office is fixed at the address stated in Article 4 of the Articles of Association, Cairo Governorate. Four: [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] Financial Compliance Officer, jointly authorized to open accounts with Wise B2B and Payoneer, execute client agreements, and represent the Company before GAFI, ETA, and NOSI. Five: Management shall complete all remaining tax, social-insurance, and operating-license registrations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance of the Arab Republic of Egypt; principal statutory portal: www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoice/e-receipt system: invoicing.eta.gov.eg (Mobil platform); customs single-window: Nafeza (www.nafeza.gov.eg).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC obtains its Tax Card and VAT registration through the following statutory sequence: (1) incorporation and file registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Ministry’s Investor Service Center; (2) filing of Tax Registration Form No. 1 with the competent ETA tax office located in the registered office’s jurisdiction; (3) submission of the memorandum of association, commercial register extract, certified copies of directors’ passports, proof of registered address (lease or title), notarized powers of attorney, bank account confirmation, and a written description of the activity (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810); (4) issuance by ETA of the unified Tax Card containing the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and, when triggered, the VAT registration number; (5) mandatory onboarding onto ETA’s e-invoicing platform before issuing taxable supplies. No minimum paid-in capital is imposed on LLC formation, and 100% foreign ownership of LLCs is permitted under Egypt’s investment regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime; LLCs are mandatorily treated as Egyptian tax residents and taxed at the entity level under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 (headline corporate rate 22.5%). Available elections include: (a) consolidated corporate tax filing for an Egyptian group where the parent holds at least 75% of the underlying entities; (b) voluntary VAT registration where annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 250,000 but is below the EGP 500,000 mandatory threshold; (c) VAT grouping election for related taxable persons under VAT Law No. 67/2016; (d) depreciation and start-up amortization elections; and (e) transfer-pricing self-correction and advance pricing agreement mechanisms, subject to ETA approval. No election exists to recharacterize the LLC as a pass-through vehicle; profit distributions are subject to withholding tax when paid to non-resident shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, together with its Executive Regulations, integrated with the Egyptian e-invoice and e-receipt fiscal digitalization framework
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 in annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services measured over any rolling 12-month period (mandatory VAT registration); voluntary registration is permitted once annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 250,000. Export-only businesses may apply for VAT registration and zero-rating even below threshold due to refund/compliance needs. Fines for non-registration range from EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 and the taxpayer remains liable for all uncollected VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA enforces a mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipt regime through the Mobil portal with real-time fiscal clearance. All VAT- and income-tax-registered persons, regardless of size, must issue XML/REST-API integrated invoices conforming to the ETA Invoice Standard (UUID, issuer digital certificate, registered codes for goods/services, QR-code digital stamp). Each invoice must receive ETA validation before being transmitted to the counterparty; B2C sales flow through the e-receipt system. Non-compliance, delayed filing, or invoices failing clearance trigger penalties of EGP 20,000–100,000 per invoice, plus potential suspension of the taxpayer’s e-invoice status and VAT refund block.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT is available where the LLC proves that: (a) for goods, the goods were physically transferred out of Egypt within 90 days from the date of supply and cleared by customs export procedures; (b) for services, the services (SEO/ASO localization and digital marketing) are supplied to a non-resident customer, are performed predominantly outside Egypt, and the benefit is consumed outside Egypt; (c) the export consideration is received in foreign currency through an Egyptian bank in compliance with Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) repatriation rules; and (d) the exporter retains a complete documentary evidence bundle for at least five years. Offshore service exports by an Egyptian-resident LLC to foreign principal/application developers do qualify, provided the contracts, service delivery, invoices, and currency remittances clearly evidence the foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Form No. 9) filed via the ACID/Nafeza national window, bearing the approved exporter reference and customs release date
Bill of lading, air waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing departure from Egyptian customs territory
Original commercial invoice and the underlying export contract/purchase order describing the goods or digitally delivered services
Certificate of origin issued by the competent Chamber of Commerce or the ETA-approved origin authority (where applicable)
Foreign-currency inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice issued by an Egyptian licensed bank proving receipt of the export proceeds
ETA export list (if applicable), freight insurance certificates, and any electronic evidence of offshore service delivery (e.g., server logs, platform analytics, delivery confirmations)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA audits export zero-rating claims with reference to the customs manifest, banking remittance records, and service contracts. Missing documentation, late FX repatriation, circular or sham export transactions, or diversion of goods to domestic consumption triggers: (a) reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of the undeclared 14% VAT on the full consideration, plus late-return and delay fines; (b) tax evasion penalties under Article 76 of VAT Law 67/2016 – imprisonment of not less than six months and/or a fine of EGP 5,000–50,000, together with an obligatory charge of double the evaded tax; (c) under Customs Law No. 66/1963, fraudulent export declarations attract fines of 100%–300% of the goods’ customs value and possible confiscation; and (d) e-invoice integrity violations subject to the EGP 20,000–100,000 per-document sanction. Refund claims may be suspended or clawed back on discovery of any false export substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) acting through licensed authorized-dealer commercial banks and the Exchange Control Committee constituted under the Egyptian Exchange Control Law No. 38 of 1994, read with the Central Bank, Banking Sector and Monetary System Law No. 88 of 2003 (as amended)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt holds IMF Article VIII status (since 2004) and, following the CBE's 2022-2024 liberalization measures, operates a market-determined EGP exchange rate with current-account convertibility for service-trade payments, subject to underlying-contract and purpose-code verification by the authorized dealer bank. Capital-account inflows are registrable with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and reportable to the CBE's balance-of-payments system; profit and dividend remittances for non-resident shareholders are treated as current-account transfers and are lawful, but are operationally gated by delivery of audited financial statements, a board distribution resolution, an Egyptian Tax Authority clearance certificate, and a 5-10 business day FX booking window at the designated bank; the post-2024 liquidity normalization has eliminated the former remittance queue, though bank-level documentary and correspondent-bank negative-news screening remains the practical hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service exporters (ISIC 7310 advertising/SEO agreement) must repatriate 100% of export proceeds through an Egyptian authorized dealer bank within 180 days from invoice date or service-provision date, whichever is later; proceeds may be retained in eligible foreign-currency accounts (EVA) and are not subject to any mandatory private-sector conversion ratio, although the CBE's export-proceeds monitoring ledger requires the receiving bank to match each credit against the underlying export contract and invoice within the statutory window, and funds may be used for import settlements or converted at the interbank rate at the client's instruction. Delayed repatriation triggers penalty interest, restricted-list placement, denial of tax zero-rating benefits, and potential hardening of the exporter's annual commercial registry renewal.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital subscription/escrow-type formation account plus multicurrency operational account (EGP, USD, EUR)
Temporary capital deposit account plus EGP operating account with FX remittance rider
Multicurrency treasury and settlement account with dedicated cross-border service-desk onboarding
Capital formation account and domestic EGP operational account
Capital contribution sub-ledger plus EGP/USD operational account
Sweep-linked dual-currency operational account with capital formation memorandum ledger
Dual-currency treasury account with accelerated AML clearance for foreign-owned digital-service SMEs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary or sole treasury rail. Wise B2B and Payoneer are not CBE-licensed banks and cannot satisfy the entity's statutory obligations for EGP tax settlement, payroll, or CBE export-proceeds repatriation; they may be deployed only as auxiliary receivables concentrators for foreign client collections, subject to a documented treasury policy requiring systematic sweeping (minimum weekly) into the Egyptian authorized-dealer bank account, with each sweep accompanied by the underlying invoice set and the funds declared on the CBE BOP declaration. Holding material balances offshore without repatriation will be treated by the Egyptian bank and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) as a potential structuring flag.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical attendance at the branch is required for the authorized signatory opening the account; CBE-regulated banks do not accept pure video-KYC remote opening for corporate accounts. Non-resident directors/shareholders need not travel provided a locally resident signatory or an attorney-in-fact under a notarized and (where required) apostilled power of attorney appears in person; the foreign beneficial owners must nonetheless submit certified identity documents and a source-of-funds questionnaire that the bank records against the corporate file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% non-resident ownership with no local director footprint and no prior banking history in Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI investment file, commercial registry certificate (Arabic), certified copy of the LLC statutes in Arabic, apostilled passports and residence proofs of all beneficial owners, signed beneficial-ownership declaration, source-of-wealth statement, board resolution appointing the local signatory/attorney, and a brief business narrative for the service line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First-inbound credits arriving from aggregator ecosystems (Wise, Payoneer, Paypal) with mixed remitter references that do not match named client invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-institution/MSB license evidence for each aggregator, the three most recent executed client service agreements, itemized invoices, App Store/Google Play performance dashboards proving deliverable completion, and a signed undertaking mapping each incoming aggregator credit to a specific invoice and client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High receivables turnover: monthly inbound/outbound flows exceeding 25% of opening balance without corresponding local payroll, rent, or tax payments within the first 90 days
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and cash-flow policy, 12-month projected cash-flow statement, NASSORA social-insurance receipts and payroll evidence, Egyptian Tax Authority filings (wage withholding, VAT Form 41, corporate income tax), and CBE purpose-code reconciliation schedules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client-base exposure to jurisdictions or counterparties flagged in sanctions or adverse-media screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed customer due-diligence files including ultimate beneficial owner declarations, UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening logs with timestamps, app-store operator registration excerpts validating the client's operating identity, AML warranties and non-crypto legal entity representations embedded in the master services agreement, and the agency's written client-acceptance policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder must transmit the capital contribution by SWIFT MT103 from its own bank account with the remittance reference 'Capital Contribution - EG_LLC (GAFI Reg. No.)' and the transfer purpose designated as 'Direct investment: equity capital (inward)' in the CBE electronic BOP declaration; the receiving Egyptian bank deposits the funds into a temporary capital subscription/escrow account, issues the capital deposit certificate required for commercial registration, and upon completion of incorporation converts or credits the funds into the entity's operating account at the prevailing interbank rate. The bank must file the inward remittance declaration within five working days, and the contribution itself is neither taxable revenue nor subject to corporate income tax.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rail for recurring cross-border vendor payments (AdTech platforms, SaaS subscriptions, overseas subcontractors) is the SWIFT MT103 sequence supported by the underlying service contract, pro-forma invoice, and evidence of Egypt income-tax withholding or tax-clearance status where applicable; domestic EGP disbursements clear through the CBE Real-Time Gross Settlement and Instant Payment Network rails, enabling same-day payroll and supplier settlement. The commercial letter of credit rail is not applicable or recommended for service-agency disbursements and should be expressly excluded from the treasury mandate to avoid mischaracterization of intangible service payments as goods imports.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (outright forwards) against the authorized dealer bank, restricted to hedging documented forecast EGP/USD service receivables
Onshore FX swap contracts (spot-plus-forward combination) for systematic liquidity alignment between EGP operational balances and foreign-currency collected proceeds
Cross-currency swap contracts with CBE-licensed banks for matched medium-term financial obligations where a written hedging policy and board delegation exist

Offshore EGP/USD NDF positions are not permissible for the resident Egyptian LLC and must be prohibited in the treasury mandate; non-deliverable exposure onshore may arise only through an authorized dealer bank's risk-transformation product approved under CBE derivative-market instructions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form No. 1 for corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Corporate Tax Sector
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year end; for calendar-year filers, on or before April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 0.75% of assessed tax per week, capped at 15%; additional fixed penalty of EGP 3,000–20,000; interest assessed on unpaid tax; repeated default may trigger enforced collection and litigation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval and filing of audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months after fiscal year end (calendar-year companies: by June 30); audited statements and AGM minutes must be filed with GAFI/Commercial Registry within 15 days of the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EGP 100,000 under Article 362 of Companies Law No. 159/1981; failure to approve financial statements for consecutive years can trigger administrative strike-off of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary date of the initial commercial registration; renewal valid for one year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs an escalating administrative fine; prolonged non-renewal risks suspension of commercial activity and deregistration from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Unified Register Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership (UBO) data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Unified Register established under AML Law No. 80/2002, administered via GAFI's Egypt Investment e-portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the anniversary of the UBO filing date; any shareholding change must be updated within 60 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 60,000–200,000 under the Anti-Money Laundering Law; bank account restrictions and denial of notarization or licensing transactions until compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social Insurance Annual Wage Census (Workforce Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30 covering the prior calendar year's declared employee payroll
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 500–5,000 plus retroactive contribution arrears and interest of up to 2% per month on understated wages under Social Insurance Law No. 148/2019.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of revenue or asset size; Companies Law No. 159/1981 requires appointment of a licensed statutory auditor at the AGM, and the tax authority conditions acceptance of the corporate tax return on submission of audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by Decree No. 110/2015 and fully converged with IFRS; mandatory for all LLCs preparing statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually reconfirm all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners via the Unified Register within 30 days of the anniversary of initial filing; any share transfer, change in control, or director change must be reported within 60 days, with supporting corporate resolution and updated share register attached.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Charges

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,500 per year (typical Cairo registered office lease and local corporate/legal agent servicing fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 500 – USD 1,700 per year (typical EGP 15,000–50,000 fee for audit of a small to mid-sized LLC agency)

stage_6.entry_description: Tax card No., commercial registry No., fiscal year, status of return.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian Tax Identification Number and the registered address of the agent in Egypt; non-resident LLCs with a PE file through the PE and identify the PE code.
